passage:
A birdwatching group invited students to observe migrating birds near a wetland. The birds stopped there to rest and feed during long journeys.
Students learned that one wetland can matter to birds traveling across countries. If resting places disappear, the whole journey becomes harder.
They also saw volunteers recording bird numbers every year. The data helped scientists understand changes in migration.
A student said the birds made the world feel connected.
The wetland was not only local land. It was one station on an international route.
Protecting nature sometimes means thinking beyond human borders. Birds do not carry passports, but they depend on many nations.
